===Etymology===
{{number box|en|0}}
{{wp}}
{{root|en|ar|ص ف ر}}
Collectively borrowed from {{bor|en|es-ear|zero}}, {{bor|en|frm|zero}}, and (their etymon) {{bor|en|roa-oit|zero}}, from {{der|en|la-med|zēphirum}}, from {{der|en|ar|صِفْر||nothing; [[cipher]]}}, itself calqued from {{der|en|sa|शून्य|tr=śūnyá|t=void; nothingness}}.<ref>{{R:OED Online|pos=''n.'' and ''adj.''|noformat=1|id=4029618546}}</ref> {{doublet|en|cipher|chiffre}}. Cognate with {{cog|es|cero}} and {{cog|fr|zéro}}.

===Numeral===
{{head|en|numerals}}

# {{cln|en|cardinal numbers}} The [[cardinal number]] occurring before [[one]] and that [[denote]]s no [[quantity]] or amount at all, represented in [[Arabic numeral]]s as [[0]].
#: {{ux|en|The conductor waited until the passenger count was '''zero'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|A cheque for '''zero''' dollars and '''zero''' cents crashed the computers on division by '''zero'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Nimi Princewill|title=Uganda’s President Museveni warns citizens they are ‘playing with fire’ over planned protests|magazine=w:CNN|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2024/07/22/africa/uganda-anti-corruption-protest-intl|date=2024-07-22|passage=Last year, it scored 26 on Transparency International’s Corruption Perceptions Index which ranks countries on a scale of '''zero''' to 100, with '''zero''' meaning “highly corrupt” and 100 signifying that a country is “very clean.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240725155405/https://edition.cnn.com/2024/07/22/africa/uganda-anti-corruption-protest-intl/}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2025-05-14|author=Andy Comfort|title=Holding out for a '''zero'''...|journal=RAIL|issue=1035|page=58|text="A '''zero''' itself is nothing, but without a '''zero''' you cannot count anything. Therefore, a '''zero''' is something, yet '''zero'''."<br> These words of wisdom from the Dalai Lama might not have been in the minds of planners and engineers when designing new railway station platforms, but for several main line stations, '''zero''' is indeed something. Eight stations in the UK now operate a Platform 0 - from Cardiff to Kings Cross, Doncaster and Haymarket.}}

====Usage notes====
* In an adjectival sense, used with the plural of a countable noun or with an uncountable noun:
*: ''I have '''zero''' dollars and '''zero''' food.''

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~|s|es}}

# The [[numeric]] [[symbol]] that represents the cardinal number [[#Numeral|zero]].
#: {{ux|en|In unary and k-adic notation in general, '''zero''' is the empty string.}}
#: {{ux|en|Write 0.0 to indicate a floating point number rather than the integer '''zero'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''zero''' sign in American Sign Language is considered rude in some cultures.}}
# The [[digit]] [[0]] in the [[decimal]], [[binary]], and all other [[base]] numbering systems.
#: {{ux|en|One million has six '''zeroes'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2007-09-11|author=John Markoff|title=Redefining the Architecture of Memory|work=w:The New York Times|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2007/09/11/technology/11storage.html
|passage=His idea is to stand billions of ultrafine wire loops around the edge of a silicon chip — hence the name racetrack — and use electric current to slide infinitesimally small magnets up and down along each of the wires to be read and written as digital ones and '''zeros'''.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20201109034838/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/09/11/technology/11storage.html}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2008-03-02|author=Tanya Khovanova|title=Autobiographical Numbers|journal=w:arXiv|url=https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.0270|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260426050402/https://arxiv.org/pdf/0803.0270|doi=|volume=|issue=|pages=1
|passage=Here is the formal definition: an autobiographical number is a number ''N'' such that the first digit of ''N'' counts how many '''zeroes''' are in ''N'', the second digit counts how many ones are in ''N'' and so on. In our example, 1210 has 1 '''zero''', 2 ones, 1 two and 0 threes.}}
#* {{quote-journal |en |date=2024-01-04 |last=Sparkes |first=Matthew |title=First working graphene semiconductor could lead to faster computers |journal=w:New Scientist |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2410612-first-working-graphene-semiconductor-could-lead-to-faster-computers/ |accessdate=2024-01-18 |passage=This effectively allows switching on and off of the flow of current, so it is either conducting or not conducting, creating the binary system of '''zeroes''' and ones used in digital computers.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240223062132/https://www.newscientist.com/article/2410612-first-working-graphene-semiconductor-could-lead-to-faster-computers/}}
# {{lb|en|informal|uncountable}} [[nothing|Nothing]], or [[none]].
#: {{co|en|'''zero'''-defect}}
#: {{ux|en|The shipment was lost, so they had '''zero''' in stock.}}
#: {{ux|en|He knows '''zero''' about humour.}}
#: {{ux|en|In the end, all of our hard work amounted to '''zero'''.}}
# The value of a [[magnitude]] corresponding to the cardinal number zero.
#: {{ux|en|The electromagnetic field does not drop all of the way to '''zero''' before a reversal.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-07-06|volume=408|issue=8843|page=68|magazine=w:The Economist
|url=http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21580518-terrible-name-interesting-trend-rise-smart-beta|title=The rise of smart beta
|passage=Investors face a quandary. Cash offers a return of virtually '''zero''' in many developed countries; government-bond yields may have risen in recent weeks but they are still unattractive. Equities have suffered two big bear markets since 2000 and are wobbling again. It is hardly surprising that pension funds, insurers and endowments are searching for new sources of return.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401153128/https://www.economist.com/finance-and-economics/2013/07/06/the-rise-of-smart-beta}}
# The point on a scale at which numbering or measurement originates.
#: {{ux|en|The temperature outside is ten degrees below '''zero'''.}}
# {{lb|en|mathematics}} A value of the [[independent variable]]s of a function, for which the [[function]] is equal to zero.
#: {{ux|en|The '''zeroes''' of a polynomial are its roots by the fundamental theorem of algebra.}}
#: {{ux|en|The derivative of a continuous, differentiable function that twice crosses the axis must have a '''zero'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|The nontrivial '''zeros''' of the Riemann zeta function may all lie on the critical line.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2006|author=Ivan Francis Wilde|title=Lecture Notes on Complex Analysis|publisher=w:Imperial College Press|pageurl=https://books.google.com.au/books?id=vrWES2W6vG0C&pg=PA153&dq=%22limit+point%22%7C%22limit+points%22&hl=en&newbks=1&newbks_redir=0&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwjOromHt6vrAhWSguYKHZ3hDKsQ6AEwInoECFUQAg#v=onepage&q=%22limit%20point%22%7C%22limit%20points%22&f=false|page=153
|passage=As the next example shows, the set of '''zeros''' may well have a limit point not belonging to the domain.}}
# {{senseid|en|algebra}} {{lb|en|mathematics|algebra}} The [[additive]] [[identity element]] of a [[monoid]] or greater [[algebraic structure]], particularly a [[group]] or [[ring]].
#: {{ux|en|Since a commutative '''zero''' is the inverse of any additive identity, it must be unique when it exists.}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''zero''' (of a ring or field) has the property that the product of the '''zero''' with any element yields the '''zero'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|The quotient ring over a maximal ideal is a field with a single '''zero''' element.}}
# {{senseid|en|person dismissed as unimportant}} {{lb|en|slang}} A person [[dismiss]]ed as [[unimportant]].
#: {{syn|en|cipher|nobody<id:person dismissed as unimportant>|nonentity|loser|Thesaurus:worthless person}}
#: {{ux|en|They rudely treated him like a '''zero'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q3274237}} {{lb|en|linguistics}} A [[difference]] that is present at an [[abstract#Adjective|abstract]] level, but not [[realized]] in the [[form#Noun|form]], that is, [[superficially]] ([[on the surface]]).
#: {{ux|en|Sometimes a difference in intended meaning has only a '''zero''' to mark it, in which case the utterance may be [[ambiguous]] when context alone does not fully clarify it.}}
# {{lb|en|military|informal|historical}} {{n-g|A casual misspelling of [[Zero]] ("a fighter aircraft operated by Imperial Japan during World War II").}}
# A setting of [[calibrate]]d instruments such as a [[firearm]], corresponding to a zero value.
# {{lb|en|finance}} A [[security]] which has a [[zero coupon]] (paying no periodic interest).
#: {{ux|en|The takeovers were financed by issuing '''zeroes'''.}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|~es,+}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[set]] some [[amount]] to be [[#Noun|zero]].
#: {{ux|en|They tried to '''zero''' the budget by the end of the quarter.}}
#: {{ux|en|Results were inconsistent because an array wasn’t '''zeroed''' during initialization.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Zero''' the fluorometer with the same solvent used in extraction.}}
#: {{ux|en|George parked in space 34, '''zeroed''' the trip meter, closed and locked his car, then went back to the guard shack.}}
# To [[disappear]] or make something disappear.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1997|author=Tom Clancy|title=Executive Orders|page=340|passage=Traffic on the encrypted channels used by senior Iraqi generals had peaked and '''zeroed''', then peaked again, and '''zeroed''' again.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2001|author=Mark Pesce|chapter=True Magic|title=True Names by Vernor Vinge and the Opening of the Cyberspace Frontier|editor=James Frenkel|passage=They discovered the object code for the simulator that was DON, and '''zeroed''' it. DON — or his creator — was clever and had planted many copies,}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=Anna Maxted|title=Being Committed|page=358|passage=If I '''zeroed''' Jack, I'd get by So I'd erased him, pretended the last few months had never happened.}}
# To [[adjust]] until the [[variance]] is [[reduce]]d to an [[acceptably]] [[low]] [[amount]].
#: {{ux|en|The soldier took his gun to the shooting range to '''zero''' its aim.}}
